verdict.rationale: Fastmail's developer page documents a public JMAP API with a published session endpoint (https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session), API-token and OAuth auth, CORS support, and full specifications in IETF RFCs 8620, 8621 and 9610. Batched method calls let a client query, fetch and send mail programmatically, so an AI-native user can drive the mailbox through it. The OpenAPI probe 404s don't contradict this, since the API is documented through RFCs and runtime discovery rather than an OpenAPI file. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of driving Fastmail through JMAP, and a machine-readable OpenAPI-style spec or llms.txt for agent tooling.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: The JMAP session resource can be found at https://api.fastmail.com/jmap/session
POST a `methodCalls` array. Query, fetch, and send, all in one HTTP request.
Standard OAuth 2.0 or Bearer tokens. No custom auth protocol to implement.
No patents. No fees. Fully documented.
